architectureDecision.pageObject: Reuse and extend pages/product-management.page.ts for verified product-form, table, dialog, search, and heading locators plus user-intent CRUD actions.
architectureDecision.fixture: Reuse the existing test-scoped productManagementPage fixture backed by a fresh adminPage context; do not add a resource or API fixture.
architectureDecision.helper: Keep only stateless title, annotation, UI setup, UI cleanup, dialog, and DOM-order helpers in the spec; all inputs and expectations stay in this JSON file.
architectureDecision.inspectionFallback: playwright-cli is not installed; locators were verified against frontend-admin/src/App.jsx and will be rechecked during script-review with standard Playwright/browser evidence.

scopeManifest.excludedReason: Out of HW4 scope — API testing: the authoritative steps require Postman/cURL, direct HTTP status or response assertions, malformed/expired/tampered tokens, non-UI payload types, or database inspection.

manualOnly.reason: Playwright-native UI automation was drafted, but the known mass-update behaviour renames every existing product. Because HW04 prohibits API/database restoration and the UI cannot uniquely identify and restore all affected pre-existing rows afterward, executing this case would violate mandatory self-cleaning isolation. Retain for HITL/manual execution in a disposable database only; do not count it as automated.

hybridClausesNotCovered: HTTP 200/201/400 response codes are not asserted for selected create, edit, delete, or validation cases.
Database persistence, database row counts, and database isolation are not asserted; only UI-rendered state is covered.
Network request presence or absence is not intercepted or asserted.
The transient loading indicator clause in TC-FR15-EP-006 is asserted only as a UI locator and is not made deterministic through prohibited network interception.
sourceDiscrepancies: FR15-test-cases.md assigns BUG-FR15-001/003 to EP-001 and EP-002 and BUG-FR15-003 to EP-003, while FR15-bug-report.md defines those IDs as zero-price, float-price, and float-price defects rather than create-notification/format/isolation defects.
FR15-test-cases.md assigns BUG-FR15-005 to authentication NEG-001 through NEG-004 and to missing-price NEG-013, while FR15-bug-report.md defines BUG-FR15-005 only as the missing-price defect.
The appended BVA coverage matrix references TC-FR15-BV-001 through TC-FR15-BV-021, but the actual BVA case headings and final total define only TC-FR15-BV-001 through TC-FR15-BV-015.
TC-FR15-NEG-006 and TC-FR15-NEG-007 contain unresolved Bug ID placeholders, so no Bug ID is inferred for those cases.
TC-FR15-NEG-024 is titled as verifying that asterisks are missing, but its expected result requires all mandatory labels to display asterisks; the automation follows the spec-correct expected result.

TC-FR15-NEG-027 is titled as checking that there is not more than one h1, which would allow zero, but its expected result requires exactly one meaningful h1; the automation enforces the expected result.

TC-FR15-NEG-028 specifies Name → Price → Description → Image URL → Category → Submit, while its recorded Passed result conflicts with the current React DOM order Name → Price → Image URL → Description → Category → Submit; the automation follows the specified expected order.

FR15-bug-report.md reports zero h1 elements, while the current React source contains a global EShop Admin h1 and a Product Management h2; the expected meaningful Product Management h1 still is not present.
TC-FR15-EP-006 records category and loading-state UI as observed, while the current React product table renders neither a category column nor a product-loading indicator.

The valid BVA cases assign BUG-FR15-001 or BUG-FR15-003 to HTTP-status and price-format observations, but the detailed bug report defines those IDs only for zero-price and float-price acceptance; the automated BVA cases therefore carry no canonical known Bug ID.
